text:
Easton Cowan has seven goals and 16 points in 20 games, one of the few Leafs whose season is going up, and his minutes are rising with it. He's in the headlines for sticking up for Auston Matthews after a hit, and he scored against Colorado this week.

Some of this will cool. He's shooting 17%, against 12% last season, and Toronto has scored 5.6 more goals than expected with him on the ice. His scoring rate (3.03 points per 60) is well above our range for a second-year winger. But the five-on-five numbers are good: the Leafs take 52% of the expected goals with him on, eight points better than without, on a team that has been losing the chance battle.

He plays fast and passes first: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 94th percentile for primary shot assists, carrying in 58% of his entries. Our range: 17 to 28 goals.
